price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: offensive five / lineup change as exposure
shot mix (rim, three, midrange, play-type shares)
methodological_questions: Can a lineup-change design detect a personnel effect on shot mix, and in which direction should it appear?
How should exposure be defined (single-player swap vs any five change) and matched to control possessions?
What confounds lineup changes with shot mix (opponent, score, clock, fatigue, foul trouble, garbage time, endogenous substitution)?
Is there enough exposure per swap type to detect shifts of about 1pp?
How can lineup and shot labels be defined without outcome-derived labels or lookahead?

historical_evidence.finding: Within-team-season on/off possession play-type shares across 73 team-seasons: with a shaper on the floor, CUT +1.353pp, PNR +0.98pp, SPOT_UP -1.248pp, DRIVE -0.542pp. Organizer POST_UP +2.331pp. Risk recorded: confounding. No validation recorded.

On N=1.07M possessions, opponent lineup (no rim big) shifted offensive mix: DRIVE +0.82pp (t=+3.3), 3PA -1.79pp (t=-5.8), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (SE 0.295, t=+0.4), PPP +0.008 (t=+1.1). Limited by small sample, and the shifts were judged weak/small.
Coverage feasibility gate passed: 90 team-seasons, 420,993 possessions. Lineup coverage varies within team and is separable from talent (|rho|=0.042). Beta not computed.
An exposure slope changed from -0.0255 with lineup fixed effects to -0.0063 without them. A same-shooter placebo on other play types gave -0.0075, consistent with a shooter-level confound.
The bonus FTA jump is mechanical (+5.08pp). DRIVE +0.31pp matched the placebo +0.33pp. Foul-trouble exposure was only 1.44% of possessions.
Descriptive play-type mix shifts by game state. The OTHER label is known to be noisy.
Descriptive after-timeout play-type shift against a same game-offense-period-minute comparison (56,423 possessions).
Inferred-label scheme changes cannot separate real adjustment from label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading an effect without lineup/shooter controls
failed_approaches.why: Confounding. The effect shrank by about 75% without lineup fixed effects, and the placebo on other play types showed a comparable slope (PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a mechanical jump and a rare exposure as behavioural adaptation
failed_approaches.why: Mechanical floor, exposure sparsity (1.44%), and a placebo that matched the effect.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred labels to detect change
failed_approaches.why: Label error. Near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting sub-1pp shot-mix shifts, even with N=1.07M
failed_approaches.why: Small effects with SE about 0.25-0.3pp on rim share. Recorded as limited by small sample and inconclusive.

evidence_establishes: [FAM:SF-PAP-007, status supported] Within-team on/off personnel presence is associated with play-type mix shifts of about 1-2pp (73 team-seasons). Confounding is a recorded risk and no validation is recorded.
[FAM:SF34, status inconclusive] Large-N possession designs can resolve some personnel-related mix shifts (3PA -1.79pp, t=-5.8), but not others (rim share).
[FAM:SF-PAP-009] Lineup coverage varies within team-season and is separable from talent.
evidence_does_not_establish: That a lineup-CHANGE (before/after substitution) design, as opposed to on/off share comparisons, detects shot-mix shifts.
That the earlier shifts are causal, since no validation or placebo is recorded for FAM:SF-PAP-007.
Whether shot-location mix (rim/three/midrange from shot distance) shifts, since the earlier records mostly use play-type shares.
The magnitude of the shifts or the required sample for a one-player swap.
own_inferences: As worded, the claim is close to tautological. Swapping players with different shot profiles will move shot mix, so a bare significant shift proves little about design sensitivity. A valid positive control needs a pre-specified direction and a dose-response relation with the swapped players' independently measured shot tendencies.
Substitution timing is endogenous (fatigue, foul trouble, score, opponent lineup, coach rotation patterns), so naive before/after comparisons risk artifacts like those in SF-TMP-009.
Using the same games to define a player's shot profile and to measure the shift would create circularity (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL / LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD). Profiles should come from held-out games.
Single-player swaps will be abundant over three seasons, so power should be adequate for swaps with a large expected profile difference. Sub-1pp effects will remain hard to resolve.
uncertainties: Magnitude of the shift and the variance of shot-mix shares per stint were not retrieved; there are no power calculations.
Substitution interval and play-by-play timestamps may misalign at stint boundaries.
Whether the shot-distance categories are reliable enough was not checked.
I did not read the full records, so details such as how SF-PAP-007 built the on/off comparisons are unverified.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I would have accepted a simple before/after lineup comparison. The records show that a personnel shift is easy to find, but also that unadjusted effects can be shooter/lineup confounds (SF-TMP-009) and that placebo and mechanical checks are needed (SF-CHT-076). They also show that small mix shifts are barely detectable (SF34). The decision became proceed_with_changes: a directional, dose-response positive control with placebo checks, rather than a bare 'does the mix change' test.

prior_work.summary: On/off analyses (SF-PAP-007, status supported) show personnel-linked play-type mix shifts, but with recorded confounding risk and no validation. SF34 shows lineup-related shot-mix effects that are partly resolvable at large N. No retrieved record tests a before/after substitution design on shot-location mix with a directional dose-response control.

risks.text: Substitutions are endogenous to score, opponent lineup, fatigue, foul trouble and clock. Shooter identity confounds the effect, as seen in SF-TMP-009.
Defining a player's shot profile from the same shots that measure the mix shift makes a positive result circular.
Player shot profiles must come from held-out games, earlier periods or other splits, not from post-substitution possessions.
Effects must be compared against fake substitution times and swaps between similar-profile players, as in SF-CHT-076 and SF-TMP-009.
Sub-1pp shifts may be unresolved (SF34 rim share SE 0.295). Swaps with small profile differences will have low power.
Several shot-mix outcomes and swap subgroups require correction.
Short stints give noisy shot shares, and stint boundaries may be misaligned between PBP and rotation files.
League shot-mix trends across the three seasons and within-game fatigue/tempo trends can mimic effects.

design.estimand: Within-team change in shot-location mix (share of FGA at rim <=4ft, midrange, above-break/corner 3) in the first N possessions after a single-player offensive swap vs the matched pre-swap possessions, tested for sign and dose-response against the predicted profile difference (incoming minus outgoing player's held-out shot-share profile, adjusted for role/usage).
design.unit: Substitution event (single-player swap, other four unchanged), clustered by team-game; alternate analysis at team-season level.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25, regular season and playoffs. Eligible swaps need at least k (pre-specified, e.g. 8) team possessions on each side within the same period, excluding stints with free-throw/timeout/period-boundary contamination, garbage time (margin >20 in the last 6 min) and multi-player swaps. Freeze the dataset version on the analysis date.
design.power: Before looking at outcomes, compute shot-share variance per stint from the data and simulate power. Pre-specify the minimum detectable shift (about 1pp on the primary share, sized from SF34's SE of 0.25-0.3pp on 1M possessions) and restrict the primary analysis to swaps in the top tercile of predicted profile difference. If the simulation shows under 80% power for that effect, report as underpowered rather than null.
design.controls: Fixed effects for team-season, opponent lineup (opponent's five or its big-man presence), period, score margin bins, clock bin and rest/minutes-played; incoming and outgoing player profile from held-out games (split-half by game parity or earlier-season data), not the evaluated stint; matched control stints without a swap at the same game time and score state.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo swaps at random times within the same stint, which should show no shift. (2) Swaps between players with near-identical held-out profiles, which should show about zero shift. (3) A reversed-sign swap (out vs in) should show the opposite shift. (4) Pre-trend check on possessions before the swap. (5) Mechanical-floor check: exclude possessions whose shot category is implied by the rulebook (e.g. bonus free throws).
design.multiplicity: Primary outcome: rim share, with direction pre-specified by predicted profile difference. Secondary outcomes (3PA share, midrange share, corner 3 share) Holm-corrected across 4 outcomes. Subgroup analyses labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the dose-response slope (observed shift on predicted profile difference) is positive with a 95% CI excluding 0 and the placebo and similar-profile swaps show nulls (CI includes 0 and excludes the main effect). Artifact if placebo effects are comparable to the main effect (as in SF-TMP-009, SF-CHT-076). Rejected only if the power analysis shows adequate power and the CI excludes the minimum detectable shift. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, rotation intervals, starters and box-score summary for 2022-23 to 2024-25, as available on 2026-11-02; derived possession graph version recorded and frozen before analysis; held-out split fixed by game parity in advance.

methodological_questions: Can the design detect a known personnel effect on shot mix (positive control)?
How should lineup-change exposure be defined and matched to control stints?
What confounds lineup changes with shot mix (opponent, score, clock, fatigue, game state)?
Is there sufficient sample size per five-man unit and exposure?
How to avoid outcome-derived labels and lookahead when defining lineups and shot categories?
args.query: Does changing the offensive five on the floor shift shot mix (rim, three, midrange), and can a lineup-change design detect personnel effects as a positive control?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull SF-PAP-007 or just finalize, and the budget allows either, so I'm leaning toward writing the answer now. The question treats the positive control as showing that changing the offensive five shifts shot mix, which would mean the design can detect personnel effects. The earlier SF-PAP-007 result already pointed that way, with play-mix shifting when the shaper was on the floor within team-seasons, though its validation was never recorded.

I'm now considering the confounding risks, like game state and opponent effects, plus the possibility that a changed five trivially shifts shot location. I'm sketching a within-team-season design around single-player swaps, with a high-rate three-point shooter as the positive control and placebo tests using fake substitution times.

I'm settling on a directional prediction for the positive control, since the claim as stated would be circular if lineup definitions include the outcome. I'm also freezing the data version (2022-23 to 2024-25) and considering a train/test split on 2022-24 versus 2024-25, with probability estimates for each possible verdict.
